(i) Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of Sanofi, and RevMed may, with the consent of Sanofi (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned), assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of RevMed; and</quote>
<parameter name="rationale">Section 15.2 meets our preferred position. We may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed consent (p0610) and, without consent, to a successor in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction or a sale of all or substantially all related assets (p0611), giving us the affiliate and M&A carve-out we require. RevMed needs our consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned, for affiliate assignments and cannot transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (p0615). RevMed permitted Change of Control assignment is conditioned on firewall protections in p0613-p0614 (acquired party stays a wholly-owned subsidiary, IP and R&D assets remain with the Acquired Party Family, separation from Acquiror Family competing programs, no Know-How exchange), which supplies much of the competitor protection the playbook seeks. RevMed mutual right to assign to a Change of Control successor without consent sits at the fallback level, and is offset by our own option to terminate on a RevMed Change of Control (Section 12.2(a)(ii), p0489). Critically, no RevMed termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a Sanofi change of control; RevMed termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation. Two minor points noted but not flagged: Section 9.7(a) requires us to gross up withholding tax arising from an assignment to an Affiliate, and post-termination royalties payable to us cease on a Change of Control of Sanofi (p0508). Each is a narrow economic consequence rather than a vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control.
